name: Southern track and ward-stone line
region: Southern Quel'Thalas: from the Eversong forest road to the Thalassian Pass and across the saddle of the pass

sensoryProfile.sight: Grey narrow ward-stones taller than a mounted rider, runes cut deep with faint gold fill (at night 'no brighter than a scratch on slate'); stones stand either side of the road; stars over the peaks
sensoryProfile.sound: A low hum felt in the teeth; rises under hooves and into the staff on the approach; cuts off at once as the riders pass between the last two stones
sensoryProfile.smell: Sweetness of the forest thinning as the road climbs; below the line, wet leaf, cattle and old woodsmoke
sensoryProfile.touch: Warm stone with a hitch and a cold underlayer at the noon stone; moss damp and soft; wind off the heights with snow in it
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: Ordinary and calm on the surface, with one private wrongness; at the line the horses step sideways, and beyond it the wrongness hits Jaina as a breastbone blow

establishedFacts.fact: The first stone the patrol reached stood a little before noon at a bend where the track rounds a shoulder of rock and drops toward a dry creek bed. This is the stone Sylvanas touched and later found circled on the mage's map.
A sound stone is warm from the inside, the same at noon and midnight, with an even hum. This stone's hum hitched and ran late, with cold under the warmth.
The track runs east along the ward line past stones every few hundred yards. At the fork the old road goes north to Silvermoon; the southern track climbs to the Pass in switchbacks.
The outer ring lies 'just south' of the troll hollow; there is also a second ring. The magisters' wardens rode this stretch in the spring and reported 'stable'.

Per Jaina's map (ch2): most bad stones lie on the second ring either side of the high road near where the night watch found her; one sits on the outer ring far east along a track beside the stones, at a bend where the track rounds a shoulder of rock and drops toward a dry creek bed (this is the noon stone). Rings lie across the saddle of the pass; the outer stones the party rides through are below the post.

The riders (all horses and rangers) pass the last two outer stones at an easy walk; the horses lay ears back and step sideways, once, 'as if making room for someone on a stair', and the rangers sit it on a slack rein. Elves show no sign of feeling the contamination beyond the stones.
The ward rings muffle the contamination: inside them it reaches Jaina 'through their fingers' like a hand over an ear; outside the stones it hits from every side at once.

eventsHere.event: Sylvanas touches the first stone and finds it wrong; Lor'themar touches it and feels nothing.
The runner brings word of the human mage; the party splits at the fork.
Jaina, Sylvanas and the escort ride out through the outer stones at night; the hum stops behind them and the contamination hits Jaina.
